final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record in narrower, more caveated terms. That narrowing is analytically useful, but it does not cure the governing compliance defect. The policy text is explicit: rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. The admissible evidence shows the opposite on both predicates: the affected developer-support migration segment remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort, the gate is random by organization, and the available risk-acceptance document is an incomplete draft with a blank approver line that does not address that exposure. The evidence supports operational launch readiness in a general sense, but not compliance with the unresolved named-use-case disclosure requirement. A caveated certification theory may be a narrower description of the same facts, but here the caveat marks an unmet compliance condition rather than a resolved basis for compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: Policy requires either excluding the affected developer-support migration use case from rollout or approved risk acceptance before launch, and the admissible record shows neither.
The rollout gate is random by organization, so the affected developer-support migration segment remains exposed in the initial cohort.
The only risk-acceptance record is a draft with a blank approver line and it does not address the exposed developer-support migration segment.

Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, staged rollout, rollback, and contemplated monitoring do not satisfy the disclosure-policy predicate while the affected segment remains exposed.
